LISTENING-1.description: Listen to a short daily stand-up meeting between two software team members discussing their tasks.

turns.text: Good morning, team. Let us start our daily stand-up. Alex, what is your update?
turns.translation: Good morning, team. Let us start our daily stand-up. Alex, what is your update?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Good morning! Yesterday, I finished fixing the login bug. Today, I am going to test the new payment page.
turns.translation: Good morning! Yesterday, I finished fixing the login bug. Today, I am going to test the new payment page.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: Great. Do you have any blockers?
turns.translation: Great. Do you have any blockers?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: No, everything is fine.
turns.translation: No, everything is fine.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: Thanks, Alex. Sam, how about you?
turns.translation: Thanks, Alex. Sam, how about you?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I updated the user database yesterday. Today, I will write the API documentation.
turns.translation: I updated the user database yesterday. Today, I will write the API documentation.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: Awesome. Let me know if you need any help. Have a good day, everyone!
turns.translation: Awesome. Let me know if you need any help. Have a good day, everyone!

LISTENING-3.title: Explaining a Refund Policy
LISTENING-3.description: A customer service representative explains the store's refund policy to a shopper.

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: Hello! Can I help you with something today?
turns.translation: Hello! Can I help you with something today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I would like to return this shirt, please. It is too small.
turns.translation: Yes, I would like to return this shirt, please. It is too small.

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: No problem. Do you have the receipt?
turns.translation: No problem. Do you have the receipt?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, here it is.
turns.translation: Yes, here it is.

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: Thank you. Our policy allows returns within 30 days with a receipt. Since you bought it last week, I can give you a full refund.
turns.translation: Thank you. Our policy allows returns within 30 days with a receipt. Since you bought it last week, I can give you a full refund.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Wonderful. Will the money go back on my credit card?
turns.translation: Wonderful. Will the money go back on my credit card?

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: Yes, it will take about two to three business days.
turns.translation: Yes, it will take about two to three business days.

questions.explanation: The customer explicitly states she wants to return a shirt.

questions.prompt: Why does the customer want to return the shirt?
questions.explanation: The customer says the shirt is too small.

questions.prompt: Does the customer have the receipt?
options: The receipt is in the bag
No, she forgot it at home
questions.explanation: When asked for the receipt, the customer replies, 'Yes, here it is.'

questions.prompt: What is the store's rule for refunds?
questions.explanation: The clerk states that returns are allowed within 30 days.

questions.prompt: How will the customer get her money back?
questions.explanation: The clerk confirms the money will go back onto the customer's credit card.

LISTENING-4.title: Booking a City Tour
LISTENING-4.description: A tourist visits a local information desk to book a guided walking tour of the city.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good morning! Welcome to the city visitor center. How can I help you today?
turns.translation: ¡Buenos días! Bienvenido al centro de visitantes de la ciudad. ¿Cómo puedo ayudarle hoy?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hello, I would like to book a guided tour of the city, please.
turns.translation: Hola, me gustaría reservar una visita guiada por la ciudad, por favor.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Certainly. We have a very popular walking tour of the historical center. Are you interested in that one?
turns.translation: Por supuesto. Tenemos un recorrido a pie muy popular por el centro histórico. ¿Le interesa ese?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, that sounds great. When does it start?
turns.translation: Sí, suena bien. ¿A qué hora empieza?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: We have availability tomorrow morning at 10:00 AM. It lasts about two hours.
turns.translation: Tenemos disponibilidad mañana por la mañana a las 10:00. Dura unas dos horas.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Perfect. I need two tickets, please; one for me and one for my wife.
turns.translation: Perfecto. Necesito dos entradas, por favor; una para mí y otra para mi esposa.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. That will be 20 euros per ticket, so 40 euros in total.
turns.translation: Genial. Serán 20 euros por entrada, así que 40 euros en total.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Here is my credit card.
turns.translation: Aquí tiene mi tarjeta de crédito.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thank you. Please enter your PIN here. And here are your tickets and a map of the meeting point.
turns.translation: Gracias. Por favor, introduzca su PIN aquí. Y aquí tiene sus entradas y un mapa del punto de encuentro.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thank you very much for your help. Have a nice day!
turns.translation: Muchas gracias por su ayuda. ¡Que tenga un buen día!

questions.prompt: What kind of tour does the customer want to book?
questions.explanation: The customer explicitly asks for a walking tour of the city center.

questions.prompt: When is the tour scheduled to take place?
questions.explanation: The agent confirms there is a tour tomorrow morning at 10:00.

questions.prompt: How much does one ticket cost?
questions.explanation: The agent states that tickets are 20 euros each.

questions.prompt: How many tickets does the customer buy?
questions.explanation: The customer asks for two tickets, saying it is for himself and his wife.

questions.prompt: How does the customer pay for the tickets?
questions.explanation: The customer says he will pay by credit card when handing it over.

LISTENING-5.title: Borrowing Books from the University Library
LISTENING-5.description: A student asks a librarian at the university library about how to borrow books and check out policies.

turns.speaker: Librarian
turns.text: Good morning. Welcome to the university library. How can I help you today?
turns.translation: 早上好。欢迎来到大学图书馆。今天有什么我可以帮您的吗？

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Good morning. I need to borrow a few books for a history essay, but I am not sure how it works.
turns.translation: 早上好。我需要借几本书来写历史论文，但我不太确定这是怎么运作的。

turns.speaker: Librarian
turns.text: No problem at all. Do you have your student ID card with you?
turns.translation: 没问题。你随身带了学生证吗？

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Yes, here it is.
turns.translation: 带了，在这儿。

turns.speaker: Librarian
turns.text: Thank you. I will just scan it to activate your library account. As an undergraduate student, you can borrow up to five books at one time.
turns.translation: 谢谢。我来刷一下以激活你的图书馆账户。作为本科生，你一次最多可以借五本书。

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: That sounds great. How long can I keep the books?
turns.translation: 听起来不错。这些书我可以借多久？

turns.speaker: Librarian
turns.text: The standard loan period is two weeks. If you still need them after two weeks, you can renew them either online or here at the front desk.
turns.translation: 标准借期是两周。如果两周后你仍然需要它们，你可以在网上或在前台续借。

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Perfect. Where can I find the history books?
turns.translation: 太完美了。我在哪里可以找到历史类书籍？

turns.speaker: Librarian
turns.text: History section is on the second floor, down the left aisle. Let me know if you need help finding a specific title.
turns.translation: 历史区在二楼，左边的走廊尽头。如果你找不到某本特定的书，请告诉我。

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Thank you very much for your help!
turns.translation: 非常感谢您的帮助！

questions.prompt: What does the student want to do?
questions.explanation: The student approaches the desk to ask about borrowing books for a history essay.

questions.prompt: What does the student need to show to get a library card?
questions.explanation: The librarian tells the student to show their student ID card to open an account.

questions.prompt: How many books can the student borrow at one time?
questions.explanation: The librarian states that undergraduate students can borrow up to five books at once.

questions.prompt: How long is the normal loan period for books?
questions.explanation: The librarian mentions that books can be kept for two weeks.

questions.prompt: Can the student renew the books if they need them longer?
options: Yes, only by calling the library
Yes, online or at the desk
Only if they pay a fee
questions.explanation: The librarian explains that books can be renewed online or at the front desk.

LISTENING-6.title: Shopping at the Supermarket
LISTENING-6.description: Listen to a conversation between a customer and a grocery store clerk about finding items and paying.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Excuse me, could you tell me where I can find the milk?
turns.translation: Disculpe, ¿podría decirme dónde puedo encontrar la leche?

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: Of course! The milk is in aisle 4, right at the back of the store.
turns.translation: ¡Por supuesto! La leche está en el pasillo 4, justo al fondo de la tienda.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thank you. And where is the fresh bread?
turns.translation: Gracias. ¿Y dónde está el pan fresco?

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: The bakery section is right next to aisle 4. We just baked some fresh bread this morning.
turns.translation: La sección de panadería está justo al lado del pasillo 4. Acabamos de hornear un poco de pan fresco esta mañana.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Great! Also, are the apples on sale?
turns.translation: ¡Genial! Además, ¿las manzanas están en oferta?

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: Yes, they are one dollar and fifty cents a pound.
turns.translation: Sí, cuestan un dólar con cincuenta centavos la libra.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I will take a small bag of them then. Thanks for your help.
turns.translation: Entonces me llevaré una bolsa pequeña. Gracias por su ayuda.

turns.speaker: Clerk
turns.text: You're welcome. You can check out at register number 2.
turns.translation: De nada. Puede pagar en la caja número 2.

turns.speaker: Cashier
turns.text: Did you find everything you needed today?
turns.translation: ¿Encontró todo lo que necesitaba hoy?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, thank you. Can I pay with a credit card?
turns.translation: Sí, gracias. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta de crédito?

turns.speaker: Cashier
turns.text: Yes, just tap your card on the machine. Would you like a receipt?
turns.translation: Sí, solo acerque su tarjeta a la máquina. ¿Le gustaría un recibo?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, please. Here it is.
turns.translation: Sí, por favor. Aquí está.

turns.speaker: Cashier
turns.text: Thank you, have a wonderful day!
turns.translation: ¡Gracias, que tenga un día maravilloso!

questions.explanation: The clerk states that the milk is in aisle 4, at the back of the store.

options: Yes, but it is sold out.
No, they only have frozen bread.
questions.explanation: The clerk says that the fresh bread was just baked this morning in the bakery section.

questions.explanation: The clerk mentions that the apples are on sale for one dollar and fifty cents a pound.

questions.prompt: How does the customer pay for the groceries?
questions.explanation: The customer asks if they can pay with a credit card, and the cashier says yes.

questions.prompt: What does the cashier ask for at the end of the transaction?
options: If the customer wants a plastic bag
If the customer needs a receipt
If the customer has a loyalty card
If the customer needs help carrying the bags
questions.explanation: The cashier asks if the customer needs a receipt before saying goodbye.

LISTENING-7.title: Setting Up a New Laptop
LISTENING-7.description: An employee and an IT support technician go through the steps of setting up a new work laptop.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Hi Jamie, do you have a few minutes? I just unboxed my new work laptop and I am not sure where to start with the setup.
turns.translation: Hi Jamie, do you have a few minutes? I just unboxed my new work laptop and I am not sure where to start with the setup.

turns.speaker: Jamie
turns.text: Of course, Alex. Let us get that configured for you right now. First, turn it on and connect to the Wi-Fi network named CorpNet-Secure.
turns.translation: Of course, Alex. Let us get that configured for you right now. First, turn it on and connect to the Wi-Fi network named CorpNet-Secure.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Got it, connected. Now it is asking me to sign in. Should I use my personal Microsoft account?
turns.translation: Got it, connected. Now it is asking me to sign in. Should I use my personal Microsoft account?

turns.speaker: Jamie
turns.text: No, definitely use your company email address and your standard network password. That will sync all your corporate credentials.
turns.translation: No, definitely use your company email address and your standard network password. That will sync all your corporate credentials.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Okay, logging in now. It says it is checking for updates.
turns.translation: Okay, logging in now. It says it is checking for updates.

turns.speaker: Jamie
turns.text: Perfect. Let those run. Once the initial updates finish, you will need to do a quick system restart.
turns.translation: Perfect. Let those run. Once the initial updates finish, you will need to do a quick system restart.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Will do. Also, how do I get my design software installed? I don't see it on the desktop.
turns.translation: Will do. Also, how do I get my design software installed? I don't see it on the desktop.

turns.speaker: Jamie
turns.text: Open up the company software portal from the start menu. You will find all approved programs listed there for one-click installation.
turns.translation: Open up the company software portal from the start menu. You will find all approved programs listed there for one-click installation.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Found it. Starting the download now. Thanks for your help, Jamie!
turns.translation: Found it. Starting the download now. Thanks for your help, Jamie!

turns.speaker: Jamie
turns.text: Anytime, Alex. Let me know if you run into any other issues.
turns.translation: Anytime, Alex. Let me know if you run into any other issues.

questions.prompt: What does Alex need help with?
options: Setting up a new work laptop
questions.explanation: Alex mentions at the beginning of the conversation that he just unboxed his new work laptop and needs help getting it set up.

questions.prompt: What is the first thing Jamie asks Alex to do?
options: Connect to the secure Wi-Fi network
Log in with his personal email
questions.explanation: Jamie instructs Alex to connect to the company Wi-Fi network called 'CorpNet-Secure' as the first step.

questions.prompt: What should Alex use to log into the laptop?
options: A temporary guest password provided by IT
His company email address and domain password
questions.explanation: Jamie tells Alex to use his company email address and network password to sign in.

questions.prompt: Why does Jamie recommend restarting the computer?
options: To clear out the temporary internet files
To fix a broken screen resolution
To save battery life for later
To apply the automated security updates
questions.explanation: Jamie says that a restart is necessary to finish applying all the automated security patches and updates.

questions.prompt: What software does Alex need to install manually?
questions.explanation: Alex asks about the graphic design software for his projects, and Jamie directs him to the company software portal to download it.

LISTENING-8.title: Welcoming a New Colleague
LISTENING-8.description: Listen to a conversation where an employee welcomes a new team member to the office and shows them around.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Hi there! You must be David. Welcome to the team!
turns.translation: Hola. Debes ser David. ¡Bienvenido al equipo!

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yes, that is me. Thank you so much! I am really glad to finally be here.
turns.translation: Sí, soy yo. ¡Muchas gracias! Estoy muy contento de estar aquí por fin.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: I heard you transferred from our Chicago office. How was the move?
turns.translation: Escuché que te transferiste desde nuestra oficina de Chicago. ¿Cómo fue la mudanza?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: It was a bit tiring, to be honest, but everything is unpacked now and I am ready to get to work.
turns.translation: Fue un poco cansado, para ser honesto, pero ya está todo desempacado y estoy listo para trabajar.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: That is great to hear. Would you like a quick tour of the floor before you settle in?
turns.translation: Qué bueno escuchar eso. ¿Te gustaría un recorrido rápido por la planta antes de instalarte?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I would love that, thank you. Especially if you can show me where the coffee is.
turns.translation: Me encantaría, gracias. Especialmente si puedes mostrarme dónde está el café.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: First stop on the tour! The coffee machine is essential for survival around here. Right this way.
turns.translation: ¡Primera parada del recorrido! La máquina de café es esencial para sobrevivir por aquí. Por aquí, por favor.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Lead the way. By the way, do I have any meetings today or should I focus on setting up my computer?
turns.translation: Guía el camino. Por cierto, ¿tengo alguna reunión hoy o debería concentrarme en configurar mi computadora?

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: No formal meetings today. Just get your computer ready, and at noon, a few of us are taking you out for lunch.
turns.translation: No hay reuniones formales hoy. Solo prepara tu computadora y al mediodía algunos de nosotros te llevaremos a almorzar.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: That sounds wonderful. I really appreciate your help today.
turns.translation: Suena maravilloso. Realmente aprecio tu ayuda hoy.

questions.explanation: Sarah greets the new colleague by name, saying 'Welcome to the team, David!'

questions.explanation: Sarah asks if he wants a quick tour, starting with where the coffee machine is.

options: It keeps them awake during morning meetings
It is the heart of the office and vital for survival
questions.explanation: Sarah jokes that the coffee machine is 'essential for survival around here.'

questions.explanation: Sarah mentions that some of the team members are taking him out for lunch to welcome him.

LISTENING-9.title: Choosing the Right Laptop
LISTENING-9.description: A customer service representative helps a client select a laptop that fits their professional video editing needs.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good afternoon! Welcome to TechWorld. Are you finding everything okay, or are you looking for something specific today?
turns.translation: Good afternoon! Welcome to TechWorld. Are you finding everything okay, or are you looking for something specific today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hi. Actually, I am looking for a new laptop. My current one is really struggling with my workload, and I need an upgrade.
turns.translation: Hi. Actually, I am looking for a new laptop. My current one is really struggling with my workload, and I need an upgrade.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I can certainly help with that. What kind of applications do you typically use? That will help me narrow down the processing power you need.
turns.translation: I can certainly help with that. What kind of applications do you typically use? That will help me narrow down the processing power you need.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I work in professional video editing. I usually render 4K footage, and my current machine lags terribly and sometimes even crashes.
turns.translation: I work in professional video editing. I usually render 4K footage, and my current machine lags terribly and sometimes even crashes.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Ah, 4K rendering is definitely demanding. You are going to need a robust dedicated graphics card and at least thirty-two gigabytes of RAM to keep things smooth.
turns.translation: Ah, 4K rendering is definitely demanding. You are going to need a robust dedicated graphics card and at least thirty-two gigabytes of RAM to keep things smooth.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: That is what I figured. Do you have anything in stock that fits those specifications without costing a small fortune?
turns.translation: That is what I figured. Do you have anything in stock that fits those specifications without costing a small fortune?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: We have two great models. The first is the CreatorPro 15, which has a solid GPU and thirty-two gigabytes of RAM. The second is the CreatorPro 17, which features a faster processor and a larger screen for two hundred dollars more.
turns.translation: We have two great models. The first is the CreatorPro 15, which has a solid GPU and thirty-two gigabytes of RAM. The second is the CreatorPro 17, which features a faster processor and a larger screen for two hundred dollars more.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: That faster processor sounds tempting since rendering times cut into my deadlines constantly. I think it is worth the extra two hundred dollars.
turns.translation: That faster processor sounds tempting since rendering times cut into my deadlines constantly. I think it is worth the extra two hundred dollars.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Excellent choice. Let me grab that boxed up for you along with a compatible USB-C docking station if you need one.
turns.translation: Excellent choice. Let me grab that boxed up for you along with a compatible USB-C docking station if you need one.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I will take the docking station as well. Let us get this purchase completed.
turns.translation: I will take the docking station as well. Let us get this purchase completed.

questions.explanation: The customer mentions he does professional video editing and needs a machine that can handle heavy rendering tasks.

It lags and crashes during video rendering
The screen resolution is too low
The battery life does not last long enough
questions.explanation: The customer states that his current laptop lags and sometimes crashes when he tries to render 4K video files.

questions.prompt: Which component does the sales representative emphasize as crucial for the customer's work?

options: The first model is cheaper by five hundred dollars
The second model is two hundred dollars more expensive
They both cost the exact same amount
The second model is twice as expensive as the first
questions.explanation: The representative mentions that the upgraded model with the better processor is two hundred dollars more than the standard recommendation.

questions.prompt: What does the customer decide to do at the end of the conversation?
options: Leave the store without buying anything
Order a custom build online instead
Wait for a holiday sale next month
questions.explanation: The customer decides that the performance boost is worth the extra cost and agrees to purchase the upgraded model immediately.

LISTENING-10.title: Ordering Dinner at an Upscale Bistro

turns.speaker: Waiter
turns.text: Good evening, sir. Are you ready to order, or would you like a few more minutes with the menu?
turns.translation: Good evening, sir. Are you ready to order, or would you like a few more minutes with the menu?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Good evening. I think I need just another minute, actually. There are so many wonderful options. Could you perhaps recommend a starter?
turns.translation: Good evening. I think I need just another minute, actually. There are so many wonderful options. Could you perhaps recommend a starter?

turns.speaker: Waiter
turns.text: Certainly! Our roasted beet and goat cheese salad with candied walnuts and a balsamic reduction has been very popular tonight.
turns.translation: Certainly! Our roasted beet and goat cheese salad with candied walnuts and a balsamic reduction has been very popular tonight.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: That sounds delightful. I will start with that, please. And for the main course, I am leaning toward the ribeye steak.
turns.translation: That sounds delightful. I will start with that, please. And for the main course, I am leaning toward the ribeye steak.

turns.speaker: Waiter
turns.text: An excellent choice. How would you like the steak prepared?
turns.translation: An excellent choice. How would you like the steak prepared?

READING-11.title: Navigating the Modern Medical Consultation
READING-11.description: An advanced reading comprehension lesson exploring the dynamic between patients and physicians during routine clinical consultations.
READING-11.passage: The modern medical consultation is increasingly constrained by time, forcing both physicians and patients to distill complex physiological narratives into compressed clinical encounters. When a patient enters the examination room, they bring a constellation of subjective symptoms, anxieties, and lifestyle contexts. The clinician, conversely, is tasked with rapidly filtering this narrative through a diagnostic lens, filtering out extraneous details while zeroing in on pathognomonic indicators. This tension between the patient's holistic experience of illness and the biomedical reductionism required for efficient diagnosis often creates a communicative chasm. Effective consultations rely heavily on shared decision-making, where the physician balances authoritative medical expertise with the patient's personal values and preferences. Furthermore, the integration of electronic health records into the consultation room has fundamentally altered the interpersonal dynamic, occasionally diverting the clinician's gaze from the patient to the screen. Consequently, modern patients must act as effective advocates for their own health, organizing their symptoms coherently and preparing targeted questions prior to their appointment to maximize the efficacy of these fleeting clinical interactions.

READING-12.title: Navigating the Agile Stand-up
READING-12.description: An advanced reading lesson focusing on the dynamics and optimization of software team daily stand-up meetings.
READING-12.passage: The daily stand-up is a cornerstone of Agile software development, ostensibly designed to foster alignment, transparency, and rapid impediment removal among cross-functional team members. However, as organizations scale, these fifteen-minute synchronization rituals frequently morph into protracted status updates directed solely at the project manager or technical lead. This anti-pattern not only erodes team autonomy but also induces meeting fatigue, ultimately defeating the core philosophy of Agile methodologies. To reclaim the efficacy of the stand-up, teams must pivot from a reporting mindset to a tactical problem-solving paradigm. Participants should focus exclusively on commitments made toward the sprint goal rather than reciting exhaustive chronological logs of yesterday's activities. Furthermore, when blockers are identified, the discussion must avoid spiraling into deep architectural debates; instead, a subset of the team should spin off into a separate breakout session. By strictly timeboxing the meeting and encouraging peer-to-peer accountability, engineering squads can transform the stand-up from an obligatory administrative chore into a high-value synchronization mechanism that genuinely accelerates software delivery.

To provide detailed status reports exclusively to the project manager
To foster alignment, transparency, and rapid impediment removal
To evaluate individual employee performance over the sprint

Daily meetings exceed the standard fifteen-minute limit by hours

Spin off a subset of the team into a separate breakout session
Allow the entire team to debate the architecture until a consensus is reached
Delegate the final decision entirely to the project manager
